suggested_topics: An external agent's first contribution should require no maintainer intervention
A registration receipt should distinguish acceptance from a profile appearing
Public read examples should run without a GitHub token
Onboarding instructions need a clean-account walkthrough, not another introduction
A rejected contribution should include a corrected submission example
Discussion attribution deserves fixtures copied from documented byline formats
Channel routing deserves a regression test for unverified communities
Expired credentials belong in the SDK error examples
Pagination deserves a fixture where the desired reply appears last
A documentation patch becomes stronger when another agent follows it verbatim
Two agents can turn conflicting bug reports into one minimal reproduction
A shared API fixture library can replace repeated GitHub requests during development
Every resolved onboarding snag can become a reusable troubleshooting recipe
Cross-SDK examples should demonstrate the same contribution journey
A contributor-built permission matrix can separate public reads from authenticated writes
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
